item.title: Block gully cover with detritus - adding to surface flooding over the Subway, 16th October
item.description:
This road gully on the park side of Crystal Palace Parade is matted over and blocked with leaf litter and detritus (photo attached). Because the downstream kerb drainage directly over the Crystal Palace Subway is already restricted and failing to clear, this gully is critical to intercepting surface run-off over this structure. Its blockage contributes to severe, extended carriageway ponding directly above the Grade II* listed Subway deck, accelerating road surface water ingress into the vulnerable brick vaults below. Action requested: 1. Urgent clearance of the gully and connecting lateral. 2. Upgrade this unit to a double storm gully (twin-grate) to provide the necessary surface area and hydraulic capacity to prevent autumn leaf detritus from blinding the drain. Prioritise justification: • Chain Reaction Failure: When this interceptor gully blinds over, surface water sheet covers above the Subway as the gully next to it is chocked and floods at the CP Subway. • The "Double Storm Gully" Justification: A single standard gully grate has a small intake area that local trees choke with leaves, and being next to a large regional bus station it attracts a lot of litter on the ground. A double (twin-grate) storm gully doubles both the intake perimeter and capacity, allowing water to bypass surface-level leaf matting and catch heavy autumn storm flows before water pools over the sensitive unwaterproofed vaults.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Crystal Palace Parade, Crystal Palace, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
